```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

FlowerTrait measures colour, pattern, symmetry and shape traits of flowers in
field photographs. This vignette runs without Python: it uses the example
photographs shipped with the package, the outlines produced by the back end and
the validation data.

```{r}
library(FlowerTrait)
ex <- ft_example_photos()
ex[, c("photo_id", "species", "country", "license", "rights_holder")]
```

## Outlines and core traits in R

The back end finds the main flower, crops it and outlines it with SAM 2.1. The
crops and outlines of the example photographs are included, so the core traits
can be computed in R alone.

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 4))
for (i in 1:4) ft_plot_outline(ex$crop[i], ex$mask[i], main = ex$species[i])
par(op)
tr <- ft_traits(ex$crop, ex$mask)
tr[, c("photo_id", "L_mean", "C_mean", "colour_name", "centre_dL", "petal_n", "sym_rotational")]
```

`colour_name` names the colour of the petal periphery. `centre_dL` is the
lightness of the centre minus that of the petals (negative for a dark centre),
and `petal_n`, `lobe_depth` and `sym_rotational` describe the outline seen
face-on.

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
ft_plot_symmetry(ex$crop[2], ex$mask[2])
```

## Decisions of the photo filter

`ft_example_results()` holds the back-end output for the example photographs.
The default rule keeps photographs with a good outline that the photo filter
rates as usable (an open flower, entirely visible and sharp).

```{r}
res <- ft_example_results()
summary(res)
res[, c("photo_id", "species", "keep", "reason", "p_usable", "p_face_view")]
```

```{r, fig.height = 4.5}
ft_contact_sheet(res, ncol = 4)
```

## How far can each trait be trusted?

```{r}
table(ft_catalogue$family, ft_catalogue$verdict)
ft_trait_info(c("L_mean", "C_mean", "hue_deg", "centre_dL", "petal_n", "sym_rotational"))
```

Repeatability can be estimated for any table with several photographs per
observation:

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
v <- ft_filter(ft_validation, "default")
r <- ft_repeatability(v[v$keep, ], traits = c("L_mean", "C_mean", "petal_L", "centre_dL", "sym_bilateral"),
                      boot = 50)
ft_plot_repeatability(r)
```

## Photo colour against reflectance spectra

`ft_reference` compares, for each validation species, the median petal colour
of its photographs with the colour computed from published reflectance
spectra with `ft_spectra_to_lab()`.

```{r, fig.height = 4}
rf <- ft_reference[!is.na(ft_reference$photo_L), ]
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
plot(rf$ref_L, rf$photo_L, xlab = "L* (spectra)", ylab = "L* (photos)", pch = 19, col = "#4A6FA5")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
plot(rf$ref_a, rf$photo_a, xlab = "a* (spectra)", ylab = "a* (photos)", pch = 19, col = "#C0504D")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
plot(rf$ref_b, rf$photo_b, xlab = "b* (spectra)", ylab = "b* (photos)", pch = 19, col = "#E8A317")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
par(op)
table(spectra = rf$ref_name, photos = rf$photo_name)
```

Photographs rank the species much as the spectra do, especially for *b*\* and
chroma, but petals look lighter in photographs than in spectra (most points
lie above the 1:1 line for *L*\*), because cameras expose each scene to look
bright. Compare photographs with each other rather than with spectra, and use
spectra or calibrated photographs for absolute colour or pollinator vision.

## A complete analysis with the back end

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ft_install()                                   # once
ft_use_backend()                               # each session
ph <- ft_gbif_photos("Papaver rhoeas", n = 200, country = c("DE", "FR"))
ph <- ft_download_photos(ph, dir = "PATH_TO_PHOTO_FOLDER")
res <- ft_process(ph, out_dir = "PATH_TO_OUTPUT_FOLDER")
face <- res[res$keep & res$view %in% "face", ]
ft_summarise(face, by = "country", traits = ft_reliable_traits())
ft_plot_colours(res, group = "country")
writeLines(ft_attribution(ph), "attribution.txt")
```
